title: The write gate reads a name the filesystem refuses alone as no path, and still denies a path too long as a whole

context.task: Stop the write gate from denying a tool whose input holds a long line of text with a slash in it. When resolving a candidate fails with ENAMETOOLONG, the gate asks the filesystem about each name of the resolved path alone: if it refuses one, no file can bear that name and the candidate is not a path; if it admits every name, the whole path is too long, a file may exist there, and the gate keeps denying.

select.heading: ADR-024 — Solo un nombre demasiado largo deja de ser una ruta (2026-10-15, autor)

problem: tools/hooks/require_boundary_validation.py examines every path-like string of a tool it does not know (class 3): a string of at most 4096 characters, on one line, absolute, starting with ~ or holding a slash. canonical() resolves it and, below the repository root, matches each name to a directory entry with _same(), which calls samefile on the spelled path and forgives only FileNotFoundError. When a name of the spelled path is longer than the filesystem admits, os.stat raises OSError with errno ENAMETOOLONG, canonical() propagates it, and main() denies with "fail-closed: cannot tell whether ...". So a prose line whose first piece before a slash is too long, such as a session brief with "y/o" in it, blocks the tool; it happened on 2026-10-15 with a start_session call. A writer whose path field holds such a name is denied the same way. The system gives ENAMETOOLONG in two cases. A name longer than the filesystem admits: no file can bear it, now or later. A whole path longer than the system's path limit (1024 bytes on macOS, 4096 on Linux) with every name admissible: the file can exist and a tool reaches it by a relative path; letting that through would fail open. The name limit is not a fixed number: on the author's macOS (APFS) a name of 260 ASCII bytes gives "File name too long" and one of 86 "€" (258 bytes) is admitted, since APFS counts characters; ext4 counts 255 bytes. A gate that counts bytes would take a legal macOS name for a refused one.
decisions: D1 The rule. In main() of tools/hooks/require_boundary_validation.py, when resolving a candidate raises an OSError whose errno is errno.ENAMETOOLONG, the gate asks the filesystem about each name of the candidate's resolved path alone. The resolved path is Path(spelled).resolve(), with spelled as main() already builds it (expanded with expanduser and, for a relative class 3 candidate, joined to the payload's cwd or the root); its names are its parts without the anchor. The gate opens the repository root as a directory with os.open (os.O_RDONLY) and looks each name up with os.lstat(name, dir_fd=that descriptor), so that what the system receives is that one name. When at least one lookup raises an OSError whose errno is ENAMETOOLONG, the candidate is not a path: the gate goes on to the next candidate, as it does for a candidate outside the root. In every other case (every name found, or not found, or refused for another reason; the root cannot be opened; or the check itself raises anything) the gate denies exactly as today, with today's message. The descriptor is closed in every case. The gate counts neither bytes nor characters.

D2 The root is the module's REPO_ROOT, read when main() runs and passed to the check, never bound as a default argument, so that a test that replaces REPO_ROOT (tests/security/test_gate_primitives.py does) is obeyed.
D3 The rule applies to writers and to class 3 tools alike. A writer whose path field holds a name the filesystem refuses is allowed: the system refuses the write itself, so nothing reaches the disk.

D4 canonical() and _same() do not change, in either hook: tests/security/test_hook_case_identity.py::test_the_two_copies_are_the_same_code compares the two copies. tools/hooks/require_contract_context.py does not change. The new code is one helper function of require_boundary_validation.py and one branch in the except clause of main() that today catches (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) around canonical(); the RuntimeError and ValueError cases, and every OSError that is not ENAMETOOLONG, stay as they are.

D5 The docstring of the hook: the sentence "A path inside the repository that the filesystem cannot be asked about is denied." becomes, word for word, wrapped like its neighbours: "A path inside the repository that the filesystem cannot be asked about is denied, with one exception: when resolving a candidate fails because a name is too long (ENAMETOOLONG) and the filesystem refuses one of its names looked up alone under the repository root, no file can bear that name, so the candidate is not a path. When the filesystem admits every name alone, it is the whole path that is too long, and the candidate is denied." The rest of the docstring stays.

D6 The hook still imports under the system Python 3.9 and only the standard library and the gate: `import errno` joins the standard imports in alphabetical order; no syntax newer than 3.9; os.open, os.lstat with dir_fd and os.close exist there and are not primitives of tools/boundary_validator/primitives.py. No text of the hook or of the tests cites a clause of AGENTS.md or an ADR: the installer copies the hook to repositories that have neither, and tests/unit/test_kit_independence.py forbids a clause citation in tools/ and in tests/.

D7 The edits of the hook come in an order that leaves it working after each one, since the hook is read again on every call, the implementer's own governed writes included: first `import errno`, then the helper, then the branch in main() that uses it, then the docstring. The tests come before all of them (red-first).

D8 The new tests go in tests/security/test_write_gate_tools.py, in a new section after T3 headed "# T6: a name the filesystem refuses alone is not a path", with its gate fixture, UNKNOWN and CONFIG (which governs src/**). Resolution stops at the first name that does not exist, and src/ does not exist in the repository, so the cases that need a real ENAMETOOLONG put the long name right under the root or under docs/, which exists. A name the filesystem refuses alone is "x" * 300 (300 ASCII bytes, refused by APFS and ext4).

D9 The test of the multibyte name builds "€" * 100 + ".md" (303 bytes, 103 characters) and skips, with pytest.skip and a reason that names the filesystem's limit, where the filesystem refuses that name alone (os.lstat of it with dir_fd on the root raises ENAMETOOLONG), as ext4 does in CI. Where it is admitted, as on APFS, it runs.

D10 The test of a root that cannot be opened makes os.open raise PermissionError for the duration of the call (for instance with monkeypatch.setattr on the hook module's os.open), on a candidate that gives a real ENAMETOOLONG, and checks that the gate denies.
D11 The validator requires a Rationale in every proposal: include it, even if the schema of validate_proposal shown to you lacks it.
D12 No new dependency and no file outside files_may_touch: in particular not tools/hooks/require_contract_context.py, no other hook, no skill, no file of docs/.

D13 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: A class 3 tool whose input holds a candidate with a name the filesystem refuses alone passes: a prose line whose first piece before a slash is 300 bytes ("x" * 300 + " y/o z"), and an absolute path to a file of that name under docs/.
Each writer (Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit) whose path field names a file of that name under docs/ passes.

An ENAMETOOLONG raised while resolving a candidate whose every name the filesystem admits alone denies, with today's fail-closed message naming the tool, the field and the cause, for a class 3 tool and for a writer.
A name longer than 255 bytes that the filesystem admits alone is not taken for a refused one: with ENAMETOOLONG raised while resolving it, the gate denies.
When the root cannot be opened for the check, the gate denies; every other resolution failure (another OSError, a symlink loop, a NUL) denies as today.
canonical() and _same() are the same code in both hooks; the boundary hook imports only the standard library and the gate, postpones annotations and parses as Python 3.9.

tests.must_catch: a class 3 tool denied for a candidate with a name the filesystem refuses alone, as prose before a slash or as an absolute path under docs/
tests.reason: at base canonical() propagates ENAMETOOLONG and main() denies every such candidate

tests.must_catch: a writer denied for a path field naming a file whose name the filesystem refuses alone
tests.reason: at base the writer's path goes through canonical(), which propagates ENAMETOOLONG, and main() denies

tests.must_catch: a gate that lets through an ENAMETOOLONG whose every name the filesystem admits alone (the whole path too long), for a class 3 tool or a writer, or whose denial no longer names the tool, the field and the cause
tests.reason: at base every ENAMETOOLONG denies with that message, and it must keep denying when the names are admissible; the test injects a samefile that raises ENAMETOOLONG on a governed path with short names

tests.must_catch: a gate that counts bytes instead of asking the filesystem, taking a legal name of more than 255 bytes for a refused one
tests.reason: at base every ENAMETOOLONG denies; the test injects ENAMETOOLONG for the path of "€" * 100 + ".md" and must keep seeing a denial where the filesystem admits that name, skipping where it refuses it (D9)

tests.must_catch: a check that fails open when it cannot open the root
tests.reason: at base every ENAMETOOLONG denies, and with os.open refused the check cannot ask, so it must keep denying (D10)

tests.must_catch: a resolution failure other than ENAMETOOLONG that stops denying, or copies of canonical() and _same() that drift, or an import outside the standard library and the gate
tests.reason: these hold at base and must keep holding: test_a_resolution_failure_denies_naming_the_tool_and_the_field, test_a_path_that_cannot_be_resolved_denies_with_the_path_and_the_cause, test_a_symlink_loop_denies, test_the_two_copies_are_the_same_code and test_the_boundary_hook_imports_only_the_standard_library_and_the_gate_at_any_depth, unchanged

commit_message: fix(puerta): un nombre que el sistema rechaza por sí solo no es una ruta (ADR-024)
